title: Adrenal crisis
stem: Resus 2. Mr Lo, 45, has Addison's disease. He has had vomiting and diarrhoea for 2 days and couldn't keep his tablets down. He is confused and weak. HR 118, BP 78/44, RR 22, SpO2 97%, temperature 37.9 °C.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on, then assess him yourself: is this an adrenal crisis?

phases.title: Treat
phases.goal: Bloods only if they don't delay it: hydrocortisone, fluid and glucose from the cart, now.

phases.title: Ongoing plan
phases.goal: The next 24 hours; the sick-day rules for him.

events.say: He is drowsier and his pressure is falling: 68/40.
events.untreated: He deteriorated and never received hydrocortisone.

notes:
Checked against the Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance on adrenal crisis (2020/2023), NICE NG243 (Adrenal insufficiency, 2024) and the Endocrine Society guideline.

Adrenal crisis is a life-threatening emergency: hypotension/shock, vomiting, abdominal pain, confusion, often with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and hypoglycaemia. Do not wait for results: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV or IM immediately, then 200 mg over 24 hours (continuous infusion or 50 mg every 6 hours IV/IM); 0.9% saline 1 L over the first hour, then guided by response; check and treat glucose; treat the trigger (gastroenteritis, infection). Take a random cortisol and ACTH before steroid only if it does not delay treatment. Fludrocortisone is not needed while hydrocortisone is 50 mg or more per day. Afterwards: sick-day rules education, emergency card, injection kit.

Perfect script checked against the Society for Endocrinology emergency guidance, NICE NG243, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Look.r: Pigmented palmar creases and buccal mucosa; dry mouth.
Steroid emergency card: Addison's, hydrocortisone 10/5/5 mg, fludrocortisone 100 microgram.

Tests.r: Na 124, K 5.9, glucose 3.1 mmol/L, lactate 3.4. "Hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia: adrenal crisis."
Sinus tachycardia, slightly peaked T waves.

steps.label: Talk to Mr Lo

opts.t: Your body couldn't make enough steroid while you were sick and couldn't keep your tablets down. We've given it by injection. When you're ill with a fever, double your hydrocortisone; if you're vomiting, use your injection and come straight in. We'll give you an emergency card and a kit.

script.say: Hello Mr Lo, I'm the emergency doctor. Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2, and two IV cannulae.
Pigmented palmar creases and buccal mucosa: hyperpigmentation; dry mouth. His steroid emergency card: Addison's, on hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone.
Venous gas and glucose, and a 12-lead ECG.
script.do: Na 124, K 5.9, glucose 3.1; slightly peaked T waves.

script.say: Hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia, hypoglycaemia and shock in a man with Addison's: this is an adrenal crisis. We don't wait for results.
Random cortisol and ACTH with the cannula, only if it doesn't delay the hydrocortisone. FBC, CRP, cultures and a stool sample for the trigger.
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV now. 0.9% saline 1 L over 1 hour. 10% glucose, 150 to 200 mL, for the low sugar.

Hydrocortisone 200 mg over 24 hours: 50 mg every 6 hours, or an infusion. No fludrocortisone while he's on 50 mg a day or more. More saline guided by his response; treat the gastroenteritis; recheck sodium, potassium and glucose. Admit him under the medical team with endocrinology input.

Your body couldn't make enough steroid while you were sick and couldn't keep your tablets down. We've given it by injection. When you're ill with a fever, double your hydrocortisone; if you're vomiting, use your injection and come straight in. These are the sick-day rules. We'll give you an emergency card and a kit.
